channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Financial Times] SpaceX and Tesla boards are exploring potential merger
item.description: Elon Musk says combining his two public companies would be a ‘good idea’ as the world approaches an AI singularity

item.title: [Politico Europe] Maybe it’s personal: Europeans worry Trump just likes Putin more than Zelenskyy
item.description: After 20 months of upheaval in transatlantic relations, EU officials fear the U.S. president dislikes Ukraine’s leader too much to push for a fair peace.

item.title: [Financial Times] Finnish president hails progress in talks about ending Russia’s war in Ukraine
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy participates in discussions in Oslo that also involve Donald Trump’s envoy

item.title: [Financial Times] Boeing wins approval for Max 10 jet in boost for turnaround efforts
item.description: Long-awaited certification will help US group compete with Airbus as airlines seek larger and more efficient aircraft

item.title: [Financial Times] Netflix gives downbeat outlook as streaming hits dry up
item.description: Entertainment giant shakes up creative leadership as viewership growth stalls and current quarter profits set to disappoint

item.title: [Politico Europe] Poland’s government votes to ease abortion laws in challenge to conservative president
item.description: President Karol Nawrocki is aligned with the party that triggered mass protests with its abortion clampdown five years ago, and could veto the government's bills.

item.title: [Euractiv] Trump says he wants Zelensky to ‘make a deal’ with Russia
item.description: "He's going to have to want to make a deal, because I don't think his people are going to stand for it any longer," said Trump

item.title: [Euractiv] Weber gears up to fight ‘political enemies’ in 2029
item.description: The EPP chief reshuffles his top team, bringing a Péter Magyar ally into his inner circle

item.title: [Financial Times] UAE official emerges as late contender to lead UN
item.description: Supporters of Lana Nusseibeh sound out UN missions for backing as official candidates struggle to break deadlock

item.title: [Financial Times] Who are the Black Bloc?
item.description: French government says agitators from the far left helped transform peaceful protests into riots

item.title: [Politico Europe] US to offer Putin face-to-face talks with Zelenskyy and Trump
item.description: Steve Witkoff will fly to Russia for discussions about peace proposals on Wednesday.

item.title: [EU Observer] The US is no longer an ally. It’s over.
item.description: Even an eventual change of American leadership doesn't mean the US's bizarre glorification of violence goes away. It is a persistent stain, constantly eroding away at the values of an open and free society. Both are worth defending here in Europe. The US has chosen its own path. Let it walk it alone.

item.title: [Politico Europe] China threatens retaliation if UK follows the EU on tariffs
item.description: China urged Britain to follow World Trade Organization rules and warned it against copying Brussels’ approach, arguing that tariffs on Chinese EVs would be discriminatory.

item.title: [Euractiv] ‘Days, not months’ to save ICC, warns Dutch MEP
item.description: Socialists’ push to award ICC Sakharov Prize exposes political divisions

item.title: [Politico Europe] French presidential race largely unaffected by unrest, first post-riot poll shows
item.description: Far-right front-runner Marine Le Pen is still ahead of the pack, and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon remains in a close race for second place.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU unlikely to send Black Sea naval mission to repel Russian drone attacks on Ukrainian grain ships, despite Kallas’ support
item.description: The EU's top diplomat has backed the idea of a Black Sea naval mission to protect grain ships from Russian drones - but this would require much more than Europe's existing Red Sea operation, while air policing might be more effective.

item.title: [Politico Europe] 5 things the EU wants to change about its Arctic policy
item.description: As melting ice opens new routes and access to resources in the North, the EU wants piece of the cake.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs push to use EU regional funds for affordable housing and climate‑proofing cities
item.description: The European Parliament called on more spending to build affordable houses, using funds for regional development that currently comprise up to a third of the present EU budget.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs open arms to UK rejoining EU to ‘correct’ Brexit mistake
item.description: Members of European Parliament from across the political spectrum are holding the door open for Britain to rejoin the union.

item.title: [Euractiv] Brussels wakes up to Arctic meltdown
item.description: Also, in tonight's edition: Kallas takes aim at Washington

item.title: [Euractiv] Limited progress after military mobility Strasbourg trilogue
item.description: Negotiators are likely to meet again in November

item.title: [Politico Europe] Après les émeutes, les plateformes dans le viseur du gouvernement.
item.description: Présenté par GSK.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Kallas buys time on EU response to US sanctions against the ICC
item.description: European lawmakers have been pushing the EU executive to take swift action over U.S. sanctions against the Hague-based court.

item.title: [Euractiv] Commission resists fisheries policy reform in new plan
item.description: Ministers and MEPs wanted to reopen the 13-year-old text

item.title: [Politico Europe] Government expected to approve Jackdaw gas field on Wednesday
item.description: Developers have been waiting for a fresh decision on the controversial gas field since January 2025.

item.title: [Euractiv] France’s sick leave costs surge as social security deficit widens
item.description: Auditors urge spending restraint as shortfall heads towards €21.8 billion in 2027

item.title: [EU Observer] EU vows to stop buying Arctic oil and gas, but drops ban from its new strategy
item.description: EU officials vowed an end to Arctic oil and gas buying, as the European Commission presented its new Arctic strategy. But while the document commits to keeping Arctic oil and gas “in the ground,” it drops the call for an international ban.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU to broach demand reduction as energy crisis deepens
item.description: Bloc's energy chief warns of 'tough winter'

item.title: [Politico Europe] Rubio insists the US isn’t trying to hurt Ukraine
item.description: The Ukrainian president complained about delayed air defense deliveries, the U.S. no longer warning of ballistic missile attacks and a slowdown in crucial Starlink services.

item.title: [Euractiv] Romania ends political deadlock with left-technocrat government
item.description: Niculescu pledged to attract investment, create jobs and strengthen Europe

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainians evacuate soldier using heavy air drone after he spent 500 days at the front, in another first-ever in the war (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,699)
item.description: While US secretary of state Marco Rubio publicly echoes Vladimir Putin’s inflated claims about Russian gains in Donetsk, Ukrainian crews on the ground are using scarce drones to snatch back their own wounded from territory Moscow says it controls.

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs back small-business exemption from costly waste-reduction compliance
item.description: Lawmakers agree requirement for agent in all EU export markets should be scrapped

item.title: [Euractiv] Brussels to seek ‘black carbon’ ban in Arctic region
item.description: Ice-melting pollution linked to dirty shipping fuel set to increase as new sea routes open up

item.title: [Euractiv] Ukraine’s Zelenskyy on mission to fix US relationship
item.description: Zelenskyy has talked to Rubio and briefed US elected officials in recent days

item.title: [Euractiv] EPP wants Black Sea security funding in next MFF
item.description: MEPs plan visit to Bulgaria’s coast amid suspected Russian drone attacks

item.title: [Euractiv] Serbia accuses EU election observers of political bias
item.description: Belgrade had previously criticised members of the EP's observation mission

item.title: [Euractiv] Kallas warns of food ‘perfect storm’ amid EU price fears
item.description: Costlier fertilisers and disrupted trade threaten to push up supermarket prices

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s €800bn defence borrowing hides a reality of every country buying on its own
item.description: In defence, the bigger the order, the longer the production line and the lower the cost of each unit. That is a big reason why Europe has long bought American, for price as much as for technology. Europe could match it by buying together and sharing out the work along the value chain.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs resist 17% cut to EU foreign aid, instead seek €25bn top‑up
item.description: MEPs insist that they won't allow EU governments to dictate the terms of the bloc's next seven-year budget, and have called for an extra €25bn in spending on the EU's foreign policy agenda.

item.title: [Financial Times] Putin’s American friends
item.description: ‘Realist’ critics of Nato echo Moscow’s talking points on Ukraine

item.title: [EU Observer] PM Babiš blames press for ANO election loss, renews calls to abolish license fees for Czech public media
item.description: Andrej Babiš vows no policy retreat after ANO's election flop. With the opposition gaining ground in a weekend senate vote in Czech Republic, the prime minister has moved to scrap public media license fees.

item.title: [EU Observer] Generation Z in France, Spain and Albania is trapped: study hard, stay poor, live with your parents. No wonder they’re protesting
item.description: From under-resourced schools in France to Spain’s housing crisis and student protests in Albania, the immediate grievances differ. Yet they raise a common question: can young people turn education into secure work and an independent life?

item.title: [EU Observer] International Criminal Court shortlisted for EU award as MEPs urge protection for its judges against Trump sanctions
item.description: The ICC was shortlisted for the Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought alongside a Tanzanian opposition leader and jailed Iranian protesters.

item.title: [Financial Times] AI debt worries spark surge in default insurance trading
item.description: Volumes of credit default swaps linked to big tech groups soar as investors seek protection against boom unravelling

item.title: [Financial Times] The unlikely winners from Trump’s Iran war
item.description: Countries from Canada to Argentina have seen surge in investment and production as buyers rush to replace supply lost to Hormuz disruption

item.title: [DW] Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
item.description: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

item.title: [DW] EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
item.description: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

item.title: [DW] Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
item.description: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

item.title: [DW] France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
item.description: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

item.title: [DW] How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
item.description: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

item.title: [DW] Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
item.description: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

item.title: [DW] Russia wants blackout in Ukraine as winter comes — Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to cut electricity and heating to civilians ahead of winter. He also called the US president's waiver of new sanctions on Moscow a boost for Vladimir Putin.

item.title: [DW] France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization
item.description: Unrest broke out in parts of France as students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets to protest high prices and inequality. Police arrested over 1,000 people amid chaotic scenes.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
item.description: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU ministers seek balance between workplace rights and competitiveness in 21st century jobs act
item.description: The Quality Jobs Act covers common standards for being able to ‘go home’ and disconnect from remote work, and limits AI's role in recruitment or scrutiny of workers’ performance.

item.title: [EU Observer] Why Spain’s Left missed the chance to unite ahead of November’s snap election
item.description: Spain’s Left has missed its last chance to unite ahead of the snap election on 29 November — a historic failure, not so much because the numbers don’t add up, but because it now fails to offer an alternative.

item.title: [EU Observer] The forgotten protests: empty shelves and blocked roads in southern Italy, ignored by the media, reveal neglect by Meloni and EU
item.description: Empty shelves and too-expensive fuel stocks are the last drop in a sea of negligence faced by southern Italians every day. Life at Europe's edges has left many feeling failed by their government, while EU policies could be making things worse.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russia’s KOSMOS military satellite stalks Finnish spy satellite, in what could see the first strike in a Ukraine star wars (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,698)
item.description: Ukraine is also scrambling to restore drone strikes after sudden Starlink limits and to repel Russian infiltrators in Dobropillia.

item.title: [DW] What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
item.description: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.

item.title: [DW] Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
item.description: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

item.title: [DW] Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
item.description: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules?

item.title: [DW] Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
item.description: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

item.title: [DW] The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
item.description: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

item.title: [DW] Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
item.description: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.
